thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty page fired: PD-12345 - service=az8-nic-monitor - symptom=intermittent NIC packet loss + control-plane heartbeats failing for a subset of hosts in az8. Escalation path: primary on-call (emma) paged.
pagerduty: PD-12345 details: urgency=high, first_trigger=1768889000, affected_zone=az8, links=<https://pagerduty.example/incidents/PD-12345>. Responders: @emma, @liam, @maria.
emma: acked. I'm on it, jumping into metrics and node state. @ops-shift-lead can you open a status incident and ping comms? :eyes:
liam: seeing ~12-18% packet loss on eth0 on three nodes (redwood-az8-n[12-14]). Control-plane heartbeats time out intermittently, kubelet reconnects a few times.
maria: grabbing pcap and logs now, tailing `systemd` and `dmesg` on the affected hosts. attaching quick snippet of dmesg:```
[1768888991.123456] NIC eth0: tx timeout
[1768888991.123459] NIC eth0: link down
[1768888992.987654] netdev eth0 entered disabled state
```
emma: ok that's consistent. Possible host NIC firmware or HW flap. We need to reduce customer impact fast. Plan: enable routing fallback to divert traffic from az8 -> az7/az9, start draining pods on affected az8 hosts, and prepare to evict if necessary. Can we do weighted diversion first?
maria: initiating weighted diversion, will shift ~40% of control-plane and serving traffic off az8 while we validate. Command I'm running:```bash
# routing-control api call
curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/v1/routing/divert \ 
  -d '{"zone":"az8","targets":[{"zone":"az7","weight":0.25},{"zone":"az9","weight":0.15}],"reason":"nic-degrade-pd-12345"}' \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CP_TOKEN"
```
liam: traffic diversion started (confirming from dataplane): "divert_id=div-9987", current weights: az8=0.6 az7=0.25 az9=0.15. Observing 30s after diversion - error rate on az8-backed requests dropping slightly.
ops-shift-lead: status incident INC-987 created: https://status.redwood/INC-987. Posting initial customer advisory: "We are investigating intermittent networking issues in az8; we've started routing mitigation. Some requests may see increased latency or errors."
emma: quick impact estimate from telemetry: overall 2.1% of requests saw 5xx in the last 5m, peak 6% for model-inference endpoints. Top impacted customers: acme-corp (elevated errors for embedding jobs), beta-inc (batch reranking jobs delayed). Not seeing broad outage yet.
liam: starting graceful drain of pods on affected nodes:```bash
redwoodctl drain node redwood-az8-n12 --grace-period=30s --evict-local=true
redwoodctl drain node redwood-az8-n13 --grace-period=30s --evict-local=true
```
maria: continuing host-level triage, pulling NIC counters and firmware version. If we see more nodes degrade, we'll escalate to full az evacuation.
emma: PagerDuty: please note ack by emma at 1768889008. I'll link runbook steps: https://internal/runbooks/az-nic-degrade. If error rate >5% for >10m, escalate to infra-eng and start reserved-capacity burst for Dedicated pools.
raj: (oncoming night SRE) acked handover note: I'll watch metrics and logs, can take handoff in ~12m. Please add any open actions and who owns them.
liam: autoscaler is stable with diverted traffic for now. I've queued a quick job to enable burst pool for az7/az9 if we need additional capacity:```bash
redwood-admin set-burst --zones az7,az9 --enable --commit=now
```
ops-shift-lead: communications note: customers updated with INC-987 summary and we added next update ETA 30m. No PII exposed.
maria: pcap shows bursts of malformed frames right before NIC resets on two hosts; opening hardware ticket with cloud provider and attaching captures.
emma: switching routing to stronger diversion to protect customers: adjusting weights to az8=0.2 az7=0.5 az9=0.3. maria, liam confirm when done.
liam: confirmed new weights active. Monitoring error rates and tail latencies. Early signal: total 5xx dropping to ~1.2% across the fleet.
incident-bot: note: routing-fallback activated by emma (divert_id=div-9987), timestamp=1768889034.
emma: documenting mitigation steps and timeline in the incident doc https://incident.internal/PD-12345. Leaving open for monitoring and provider follow-up. I'll hand to raj in 12m for watch and possible re-open if nodes degrade further.
raj: ack - taking over monitoring at 1768889060, will escalate to infra-eng if packet loss >10% or 5xx >5% sustained for 10m.
emma: thanks team. Final quick checklist: 1) provider ticket opened, 2) routing fallback active, 3) pods drained on affected hosts, 4) customers notified. Will close once provider confirms root cause or nodes restored. :white_check_mark: 
incident-bot: PD-12345 status update: acknowledged, mitigations active, owners assigned: emma (lead), raj (handoff), infra-eng (provider escalation).
